churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting and configuration are cleanly isolated and nothing depends on internals, but the pervasive `any` (instead of generated route types and typed API shapes) plus a copy-pasted not-found convention mean both requirement changes and framework upgrades ripple through every route.

findings.issue: Loader, meta and component arguments are typed `any` in all four entity routes; the framework's generated route types (./+types/*) are configured in tsconfig but never imported, so param and loaderData changes break at runtime instead of compile time.
findings.suggestion: Import `type { Route } from './+types/<route>'` and use `Route.LoaderArgs`/`Route.ComponentProps`, and add a `typecheck` script (`react-router typegen && tsc`) for CI.

findings.issue: Missing records are handled by returning a `{ notFound: true }` sentinel, duplicated across four loaders plus a matching branch in each route's `meta`, and it never yields an HTTP 404 status.
findings.suggestion: Follow the documented pattern: `throw data('Not Found', { status: 404 })` from the loader and render one shared `ErrorBoundary`/not-found UI, which also sets the response status.

findings.issue: The data layer caches and maps `any` (`Promise<any>`, `(entry: any)` at :274,295-310,430,455), so the upstream API shape is untyped at the server boundary.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI response shapes so schema changes surface as compile errors at the single data-access module.

findings.issue: No `ErrorBoundary` export anywhere in the app; an API failure renders the framework's generic error page.
findings.suggestion: Add a root `ErrorBoundary` rendering the app's own chrome with a link back to `/`.

findings.issue: TypeScript pinned to the ^5.9 line while TS 7.0.2 has been stable since Aug 2026 and @react-router/dev 8.3+ explicitly supports typescript@7.
findings.suggestion: Move devDependencies to typescript@7 for the native compiler, keeping the same tsconfig.

findings.issue: `idFromUrl` hand-rolls regex URL parsing while the same codebase already uses `URL` objects (api.server.ts:18-24).
findings.suggestion: Parse with `new URL(url).pathname` and split on `/`, keeping one shared helper.

findings.issue: `cardSprite` hard-codes the `id <= 1025` snapshot boundary; species added by live-data updates each cost an extra per-card fetch.
findings.suggestion: Treat the sprite pattern as a fallback only, or derive the boundary from the species index rather than a magic constant.

findings.issue: Server-side fetches have no `AbortSignal` or timeout; a slow API call blocks the loader indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Thread `request.signal` from the loader into `fetch(url, { signal })` so abandoned requests are cancelled.

summary: A framework-current, dependency-lean SSR app: React Router 8.5.1 (the newest stable), hand-rolled platform usage, and clean isolation of data access behind one server module. The main aging risk is that it bypasses the framework's generated route types and documented data()/ErrorBoundary not-found pattern in favour of `any`-typed loaders and a copy-pasted `{ notFound: true }` sentinel. Those are cheap fixes now and would make it a reference-quality Framework Mode app.

apis.replacement: Not deprecated but unused: import `type { Route } from './+types/<route>'` and use `Route.LoaderArgs`/`Route.ComponentProps` per reactrouter.com/how-to/route-module-type-safety
throw data('Not Found', { status: 404 }) + route ErrorBoundary (current documented pattern)
